2612| **Escalation**
2613| 
2614| When two regions are affected, the incident commander takes over coordination, and you keep working the procedure. A problem that returns within a day goes to the data lead, even if each occurrence was fixed quickly. The second line for this section is the data team; outside their hours, the duty manager decides.
2615| 
2616| **Notes**
2617| 
2618| - A silenced alert must have an owner and an end time.
2619| - This procedure was written for eu-west; the other regions differ only in their host names.
2620| - Most false alarms here come from deployments of search.
2621| - Write down what confused you, and send it to the data team: the section is fixed from such notes.
2622| - The duty manager can extend a change window, but not open one.
2623| 
2624| ## 7.3 Database failover
2625| 
2626| Use this section when the primary database at 10.4.2.17 stops answering. The usual sign is a rising count of "Connection timeout" errors to 10.4.2.17 in the service log, followed by the alert `db-primary-unreachable`. Failover is automatic: the steps below confirm that it happened, and record it.
2627| 
2628| **Procedure**
2629| 
2630| 1. Confirm that the primary is unreachable: the service log shows connection timeouts to 10.4.2.17, and the alert `db-primary-unreachable` is firing.
2631| 2. Do not restart the services. The connection pool fails over to the replica at 10.4.2.18 on its own, and logs a FATAL line when it starts.
2632| 3. Check that the replica was promoted: the service log must show "Replica 10.4.2.18 promoted to primary" within one minute of the FATAL line.
2633| 4. Watch the service log for five minutes after the promotion. Connection timeouts to 10.4.2.17 must stop; if they go on, page the database on-call.

3510| 
3511| **Notes**
3512| 
3513| - Dashboards lag by about a minute; the log does not.
3514| - Do not rely on memory for commands: copy them from the tooling page, where they are kept current.
3515| - Keep the incident channel for actions and facts; discussion goes in a thread.
3516| - Never try a fix on all instances at once.
3517| - A drill of this section is run twice a year.
3518| 
3519| ## 9.5 Regional failover
3520| 
3521| It describes regional failover as the network team runs it today, in us-east and in the other regions. The section assumes that you can open the Edge traffic dashboard and the service log of api-gateway. The procedure is short on purpose: longer versions were tried, and were not followed under pressure. The aim is to restore service first and to understand the cause second.
3522| 
3523| Past incidents on this subject are linked from the review archive, newest first. The thresholds were set from a quarter of normal traffic, and are wrong for the week of a sale. Timeouts between services are set to five seconds, and a request that waits that long is counted as failed. A change made in the last 5 minutes is the most likely cause, so look at the release tracker before anything else. When two alerts fire together, treat the one nearer the database as the cause until shown otherwise. The network team owns the alert thresholds, and reviews them every quarter against the pages they caused.
3524| 
3525| **Signals**
3526| 
3527| - The Edge traffic dashboard shows the error rate of api-gateway above 2%.
3528| - The release tracker shows a deployment of api-gateway in the last 10 minutes.
